subject: Plotting 95% credible intervals on model covariates summary

messages.author: de3190e0e6f4a690
messages.subject: Plotting 95% credible intervals on model covariates summary
parts:
Hi all,

I'm plotting the results of the effects of different covariates from my model and trying to plot the range of the 95% credible interval for each one, as this would be useful to include the explanation of results.

Does anyone know how to do this?

I have attached the graphs, to which I'm trying to add the credible intervals, and the code I used to get here.

NF <- names(Nest_fit$marginals.fixed)

for(i in 1:length(NF)) flist[[i]] <- plot(Nest_fit, NF[i])

multiplot(flist[[1]], flist[[2]],flist[[3]], ,flist[[3]], ,flist[[4]], flist[[5]], flist[[6]], flist[[7]], flist[[8]], cols=2) ## Will generate something similar to figure *

Thanks for your help.

Cheers,
Sol

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Plotting 95% credible intervals on model covariates summary
parts:
its kind of straight forward to do this yourself, as long as you know
the internal format.

> r=inla(y~1,data=data.frame(y=0))
> m = inla.smarginal(r$marginals.fixed[[1]])
> plot(m, type="l")
> q = inla.qmarginal(c(0.025,0.975), m)
> abline(v=q)
> str(m)
List of 2
$ x: num [1:1125] -0.219 -0.219 -0.218 -0.218 -0.217 ...
$ y: num [1:1125] 2.67e-05 3.52e-05 4.57e-05 5.84e-05 7.34e-05 ...

so a marginal density, is just a set of (x,y)'s, so location x and
density value y. you can check out

?inla.marginal

for help functions, but from this, you should be able to make any plot
you like

H
